law.catch_line: Licenses to nonprofit libraries, archives or educational institutions

text.section:
The provisions of subsection (a) may be varied by a term in a standard form contract only if:
the term varying the provision is conspicuous;
the nonprofit library, archive or educational institution specifically manifests assent to the term pursuant to subsection (c) of § 59.1-501.12; and
where the term is not made available to the nonprofit library, archive or educational institution before it orders the tangible copy of the computer information:

the nonprofit library, archive or educational institution knew or had reason to know that terms would follow when it ordered the copy; and
the nonprofit library, archive or educational institution is given the right to return the copy in the event that it refuses the contract and the right to be reimbursed for any reasonable expenses incurred in complying with the licensor's instructions for returning or destroying the computer information, or in the absence of such instructions, the reimbursement of expenses incurred for return postage or similar reasonable expense in returning the computer information.

Nothing in this section shall be construed to:
alter the burden of proof in an infringement, contract or other action;
authorize making the informational content available on a computer network server or other system for simultaneous access and use by multiple users; or
limit any defense that a term of a contract violates a fundamental public policy pursuant to § 59.1-501.5 including any such policy under the federal copyright law.

For purposes of this section, the terms "nonprofit library, archive or educational institution" have the same meaning as used in sections 108, 109 and 110 of the Copyright Act, 17 U.S.C. §§ 108, 109, and 110.
